title: Friedrich Schiller's birth chart
metaDescription: Friedrich Schiller's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.8° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: the Sun and Jupiter within 0.6°, identity wired to expansion. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 17.8° Scorpio — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Scorpio and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 20.8° Scorpio, Venus was at 29.6° Libra, Mars was at 1.8° Virgo. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Jupiter — a sextile holding at 0.6°. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Mercury square Neptune at 1.1°, and the Sun square Neptune at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. Venus in Libra at 29.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 18.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements water 4, earth 2, fire 2, air 1; modalities mutable 4, fixed 3, cardinal 2. Venus, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.1° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
